html:
Here is NGC281, also called the "Pacman" nebula.

NGC281 is an emission nebula made of ionized hydrogen atoms. At the center is the open cluster IC 1590, containing about 50 stars. This whole thing is located in the constellation Cassiopeia at a distance of 9500 light-years. The bright cheese-yellow star on the right is Shedar ;-) .



Technical details
Date: 2009-11-11
Temperature: 0 to -5 degrees celsius.
Telescope: Takahashi SKY90 II with dedicated f 4.5 focal reducer (407mm focal length)
Sensor: Canon 40D unfiltered
Filter: IDAS-LPS (to counter light pollution)
Mount: LX200 10" f 6.3 Classic
Guiding: QHY5 and PHD

35 frames of 300 seconds ( 5 rejected), 40 darks, 40 flats
Calibrated and stacked in Nebulosity
Processing in Photoshop
